clue.text: As one would expect, there's something to revere inside them

definitions.text: As one would expect, there's something to revere inside them

parts.words: As one would expect, there's something to revere inside them
parts.note: Buddhist temple towers naturally house relics and images to be worshipped; the word itself also holds a deity, G-O-D, in its middle

explanation.surface: A wry remark that a building, as expected, contains something worth revering.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the buildings, and slyly notes that the letters G, O, D sit inside the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Pagodas are tiered Asian temple towers built to enshrine sacred relics.

clue.text: Colour that suits farmworkers to a T!

parts.note: pigmen are farm labourers who look after pigs

explanation.surface: A colour that suits farm labourers perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a T' looks like the idiom for 'exactly', but the T is simply added after the farmworkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigment is a substance that gives paint or tissue its colour.

clue.text: Hoarse sounding green-headed bird

indicators.note: headed asks for the head, the first letter, of the word green

parts.note: the ruff is a wading bird

explanation.surface: A bird with a green head and a harsh cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green-headed' gives the first letter of 'green', G, ahead of the wading bird RUFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A gruff voice is low, rough and husky.

clue.text: Repetitive training that's boring

explanation.surface: Monotonous exercises that bore the trainees.
explanation.definitionFit: Military drill is training by repetition, and drilling also means boring a hole.

clue.text: Indicate there's a second query

parts.note: how is a question word

explanation.surface: Someone signals that they have another question.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something is to point it out or demonstrate it.

clue.text: Springs on quiet cats

parts.note: P stands for piano, quiet in music
an ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat

explanation.surface: Something leaps on cats that are keeping silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ounce' is an old name for the snow leopard, not the weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring on prey is to jump on it suddenly.

clue.text: Cadet's syncope trouble at this ceremony?

definitions.text: Cadet's syncope trouble at this ceremony?

parts.words: Cadet's syncope trouble at this ceremony?
parts.note: a cadet who faints at his graduation parade suffers a loss of consciousness at the very event named by that phrase

explanation.surface: A young officer cadet keels over during a formal parade.
explanation.walkthrough: Syncope is the medical word for fainting; the graduation parade of military cadets is named for the same phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The graduation parade of cadets shares its name with fainting, both being a loss of consciousness and a formal leaving.

clue.text: Cryptic clues about number of relatives

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go round the number
cryptic means puzzling or disguised, so the following word is scrambled

explanation.surface: Puzzling clues dealing with how many family members someone has.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic' turns CLUES into UCLES, which goes 'about' N.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncles are male relatives: a parent's brothers.

clue.text: Look out! It has a high tar content

definitions.text: Look out! It has a high tar content

parts.words: Look out! It has a high tar content
parts.note: a lookout post high on a mast holds a sailor, a jack tar, so its contents are a tar placed high up

explanation.surface: A warning about something with dangerous levels of tar, like cigarettes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tar' is an old word for a sailor; the 'high tar content' is the sailor perched at the masthead as lookout.
explanation.definitionFit: The crow's nest is the lookout platform at the top of a ship's mast.

clue.text: Wins out, after getting led astray by cheat

indicators.note: after getting places the first scramble ahead of the second
out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of wins are rearranged
astray means off course, so the letters of led are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone tired out after being misled by a con artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns WINS into SWIN and 'astray' turns LED into DLE; the two joined give the word for cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: To swindle is to cheat someone out of money by deceit.

clue.text: Slug out in horribly sticky conditions

indicators.note: horribly suggests something mangled, so these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A slug crawling about in nasty, slimy conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' signals an anagram of SLUG OUT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Glutinous means gluey, like paste.

clue.text: A part of Asiatic holiday wear — for ladies

indicators.note: A part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something to wear on a holiday in Asia, for women.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across asiatiC HOLIday.
explanation.definitionFit: A choli is a short-sleeved bodice worn under a sari by Indian women.

clue.text: Measure fellow of advanced years, for shroud

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of measure
old means of advanced years

explanation.surface: Measuring an elderly man for his burial shroud.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printing measure, half an em.
explanation.definitionFit: To enfold is to wrap or envelop completely, as a shroud does.

clue.text: Sick — expired having imbibed quantities of salt water

indicators.note: having imbibed means taking in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: expired means died
seas are large bodies of salt water

explanation.surface: Someone fell ill and died after drinking seawater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having imbibed' puts SEAS inside DIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Diseased means affected by illness.

clue.text: It's not difficult, Holmes explained

parts.note: Sherlock Holmes was famously quoted as telling Watson that a deduction was simple, with his dear Watson tagged on

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes tells Watson that his deduction was easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary means basic and simple, the word attributed to Holmes.

clue.text: The skill to know only the cog needs changing

indicators.note: needs changing says the letters of these words must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A mechanic's know-how: just replace the cog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs changing' signals an anagram of ONLY THE COG.
explanation.definitionFit: Technology is applied scientific skill and know-how.

clue.text: Made a soldier study text

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study
a script is a written text

explanation.surface: A recruit was turned into a soldier after studying a manual.
explanation.definitionFit: To conscript is to enlist someone compulsorily into the army.

clue.text: We are quickly as used to be

explanation.surface: A note that we are, as we once were.
explanation.definitionFit: We're is the shortened form of 'we are'; were is the past tense of 'are', meaning used to be.

clue.text: Study a tail that's peculiar to molluscs

parts.note: a den is a private study room

indicators.note: peculiar means odd, so the letters of a tail are scrambled

explanation.surface: Examining an odd tail found on shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's peculiar' rearranges A TAIL into TALIA after DEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentalia are tusk shells, tube-shaped marine molluscs.

clue.text: She goes East initially, then comes back

indicators.note: initially says this letter comes first
comes back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: and can mean then, as in 'and next'

explanation.surface: A woman travels east first, then returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes back' turns AND into DNA after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna is a woman's name.

clue.text: Little creature we blame wrongly

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A small animal is unjustly accused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' signals an anagram of WE BLAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe-lamb is a young female sheep.

clue.text: Cheekily suggest receiving union leader, to make an impression

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so letters go inside

parts.note: to imply is to suggest

indicators.note: leader asks for the first letter of union

parts.note: to dent is to make an impression in a surface

explanation.surface: Rudely hinting at taking in a trade union boss to impress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' puts U (the first letter of 'union') and DENT inside IMPLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudently means in a cheeky, disrespectful way.

clue.text: Three feet on one limb aboard

definitions.text: Three feet on one limb aboard

indicators.note: on in a down clue places one piece above the next

parts.note: a yard is three feet
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: A creature balancing on one leg on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Each end of a ship's yard (a spar) is its arm, so the word describes itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardarm is either end of a sailing ship's yard, the spar from which sails hang.

clue.text: Trouble becoming prevalent after arrival of holy man

indicators.note: after arrival of puts the holy man first

parts.note: ST is short for saint
rife means widespread

explanation.surface: Unrest spreads once a holy man comes.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife means conflict or discord.

clue.text: Stirring, after leaving last of garlic inside

indicators.note: inside places one piece within another

parts.note: exiting means leaving

indicators.note: last of asks for the final letter of garlic

explanation.surface: Excited about stirring in garlic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts C, the last letter of 'garlic', inside EXITING.
explanation.definitionFit: Exciting means stirring the emotions.

clue.text: He asserts it no longer has buying power

explanation.surface: A man claims that a coin has lost its value.
explanation.definitionFit: One who states something asserts it; a stater was an ancient Greek coin, now worthless.

clue.text: He leaves the south, about to make a plea for work

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the remaining letters go round the plea
leaves means departs, so these letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: to ask is to make a plea

explanation.surface: A man leaves the south to petition for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: THE without HE is T; with S that makes TS, which goes 'about' ASK.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks are pieces of work to be done.

clue.text: Read items — take from them this passage

indicators.note: take from them says the answer is a run of letters taken from inside the words named

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Instructions to read some entries and extract this section.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'them this passage' as the definition, but only 'passage' defines; 'take from them' is the hiding signal over reAD ITems.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal passage into a mine.

clue.text: Jailbird — with presenting this plea badly a contributive factor

indicators.note: badly means the letters are disordered
a contributive factor means a part of the word, so a run of letters is taken from inside it

explanation.surface: A convict's excuse, poorly presented, plays a part in his conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: AILBI is taken from inside jAILBIrd, and 'badly' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a defence plea that one was elsewhere.

clue.text: Moreover, I left USA in confusion, for a place in Spain

parts.note: and can mean moreover

indicators.note: in confusion means the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone, besides, abandoned America in turmoil for Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in confusion' jumbles I, L (left) and USA into ALUSI, between AND and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Andalusia is a region in southern Spain.

clue.text: Assault current supplier

explanation.surface: An attack on an electricity provider.
explanation.definitionFit: Battery is unlawful physical attack, and a battery supplies electric current.

clue.text: Managed to get most back around the beam

indicators.note: around means the reversed word surrounds another
back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
ran means managed

explanation.surface: A manager gets the most out of a building beam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns MOST into TSOM, which goes 'around' RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal crossbar or beam, as above a door.
